approachQuestion.prompt:
Redundant protection ranges

Each of n closed protection ranges [start,end] has a distinct input index. Mark a range redundant if some OTHER range contains all its points. Equal ranges contain one another, so every copy in a duplicate group is redundant. Return one Boolean per input index. Ranges are unsorted and immutable.

Input: ranges = [[2,8],[3,5],[2,8],[9,10]]
Output: [true,true,true,false]

Input: ranges = [[1,4],[2,6],[3,7]]
Output: [false,false,false]

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ start ≤ end ≤ 1000000000. Use comparison-based ordering. Choose the best worst-case time; write flags in original order.

options.text: Copy indexed ranges, sort by start ascending then end descending, and process identical ranges as a group. Mark a whole group redundant if it has multiple members or its end is at most the greatest end of earlier groups. Then update that greatest end.
options.feedback: Earlier groups start no later. Their maximum end proves containment, while equal-start longer ranges appear first. Grouping duplicates allows every equal copy, including the first, to be recognized.

options.text: Sort by start ascending then end ascending; mark a range only if its end is at most the greatest end already seen.
options.feedback: For [[1,3],[1,8]], the shorter range is visited before its container and is left unmarked. Duplicate first copies are also missed.

options.text: Sort by start ascending then end descending, handle duplicate groups, but compare each group’s end only with the immediately previous distinct group’s end.
options.feedback: For [[1,10],[2,3],[4,5]], [4,5] is contained by [1,10] although not by its immediate predecessor. The greatest earlier end must survive nested ranges.

options.text: For each range, test every other indexed range for containment and set its flag if any test succeeds.
options.feedback: The answer is correct, including equal copies, but repeated all-pairs checks waste the ordering structure. A sorted scan can carry the needed boundary summary.

feedback.reason: Choose tie order and group duplicates so containment is decided from a persistent maximum endpoint.
details: Create indexed copies and sort them with iterative bottom-up merge sort by start ascending and end descending. Scan equal-range groups, retain the greatest prior end, and write flags directly into the returned array at original indices.

Sort equal starts by descending end so a containing range precedes contained ones. Exact duplicates need group handling to respect the task's redundancy rule rather than arbitrarily declaring the first duplicate unique.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For grouped-containment-scan, n is the range count. Include indexed copies and the sorting buffer, excluding the returned flags. Choose the tightest standard worst-case pair.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)
Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)

feedback.reason: Indexed sorting and equal-range grouping precede one maximum-end scan.
details: Comparison sorting takes O(n log n); grouping and flag assignment take O(n). Indexed copies and reusable merge buffer take O(n) auxiliary space. The maximum prior end and group boundaries use constant extra state.
Iterative merge sort; indexed copy; output flags excluded; duplicates grouped.
“Time O(n²), auxiliary space O(1)”: All-pairs containment is a different method. Here sorting and one grouped scan suffice, and copied records must also be counted.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(n)”: The sorted order is not supplied; comparison sorting must precede the scan.
“Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)”: Indexed copies and the reusable merge buffer take linear auxiliary memory; returned Boolean flags are the excluded output.
